_meta.project: instex Spectrograph Explorer presets -- round 5: SDSS 2.5 m / APOGEE (APOGEE-N; APOGEE-S on the du Pont as a variant)
_meta.companion: data/presets_sources.json, data/presets_sources_2.json, data/presets_sources_3.json (rounds 1-3) and data/round4/*.json; same structure. 'recommended_preset' is a dict keyed by preset (apogee_n, apogee_s); 'preset_values' collects the numbers with references ('ref') to the params that source them. Top-level 'multiplex' holds the objects-per-exposure row.
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc, and a short quote from the saved document. derived = arithmetic done here from sourced values; is_derived marks a headline value that is itself arithmetic. alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). Every quote was machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text (whitespace/glyph-normalised).
_meta.quote_normalisation: Quotes copied from pdftotext (layout and raw) and tag-stripped HTML text; the double prime (rendered '00' by pdftotext in W19), degree glyph U+25E6, tilde-operator, minus/en dashes, curly quotes and Greek mu normalised; all whitespace ignored; line-break hyphens tried both kept and joined; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces; table rows quoted as whitespace-separated cells (superscript note letters stay attached, e.g. 'Mirrorg').

apogee.title: Sloan 2.5 m / APOGEE-N (and du Pont 2.5 m / APOGEE-S): cryogenic fibre-fed H-band spectrograph, 300 fibres, uncorrected-Schmidt collimator mirror, three-segment mosaic VPH grating in Littrow, six-element Si/fused-silica camera, three H2RG arrays side by side

recommended_preset.apogee_n: APOGEE-N on the Sloan 2.5 m: D = 2.5 m; F = 3.85 into the collimator (the spectrograph's aperture stop, the VPH mask, clips beams faster than f/3.85, and the camera is f/1.3 at that beam; the fibres take f/5 from the telescope and emit ~f/3.5 at 95% encircled energy); 120 um core = 2.0" on the sky at f/5, entered as the slit of equal line width (sqrt3/2) x 120 um = 103.9 um = 2.227" at f/3.85 on 2.5 m (DERIVED; the 2.0" sky value belongs to f/5); 300 spectra on the detector (about 230 science + 35 sky + 35 telluric standards); collimator = Mirror (spherical, on-axis 'uncorrected Schmidt'), f_col = 1053.6 mm (R/2 of the 2107.22 mm cold radius, DERIVED), W = 273.7 mm (f_col/3.85, DERIVED; VPH mask 272.8 mm); camera f = 356 mm (measured warm), f/1.3; transmission (VPH) grating, G = 1009.345 /mm (as recorded; design 1008.6 /mm cold), order 1, alpha = 54.061 deg (design 54 deg), Littrow wavelength 1.6043 um (DERIVED); the real camera sits at the Littrow deviation 2 x 54.061 = 108.122 deg with the detector mosaic off-axis, so for the explorer's centred detector use lamC = 1.6158 um (the wavelength at the mosaic centre, DERIVED), beta = 55.21 deg, camera angle alpha + beta = 109.27 deg (DERIVED); detector 3 x Teledyne H2RG 2048 x 2048 x 18 um side by side along the dispersion with 2.9 mm (161 px) gaps: Nx = 6466 px if the gaps are entered as dead pixels (3 x 2048 + 2 x 161.1, DERIVED; reproduces the outer edges) or 6144 px with the gaps not modeled; Ny = 2048; pixel 18 um. Validate: chips 1.514-1.581 / 1.585-1.644 / 1.647-1.696 um (DERIVED model edges with the 2.9 mm gaps: 1.5139-1.5805 / 1.5855-1.6439 / 1.6482-1.6963 um); dispersion 0.326 / 0.282 / 0.235 A/px (the model gives 0.3257 / 0.2858 / 0.2354 A/px at the chip centres 1.548 / 1.616 / 1.674 um); R median 22,800 / 23,700 / 22,000 (blue / green / red; nominal 22,500; model slit-limited R with the slit-equivalent width 26,850-28,940 at 1.54-1.66 um, i.e. 14-32% above the measured values); spectral fibre image ~1.7 px at 1.53 um to ~3.0 px at 1.68 um (model 1.72 / 2.51 px slit-equivalent; 1.99 / 2.90 px full core); fibre pitch 6.6 px (model 6.57 px).
recommended_preset.apogee_s: APOGEE-S on the du Pont 2.5 m (a near-copy of APOGEE-N): same D = 2.5 m, same fibre (120 um = 1.31" on the sky at f/7.5; FRD expected to speed the f/7.5 input to roughly the APOGEE-N output beam, so keep F = 3.85 and the same slit-equivalent 2.227"), same collimator, camera and detector format; two-panel VPH (as-built line density NOT FOUND; use the APOGEE-N values) with a 29.2" correction wedge on one panel. Validate against the lower APOGEE-S resolution (W19 Table 13: medians 20,100-23,700 blue, 20,900-24,800 green, 19,800-21,000 red). Per-chip coverage and dispersion for APOGEE-S were NOT FOUND.

not_found: Cold (77 K) camera focal length: only 'a measured focal length of 356 mm at room temperature' (W19 Sec. 4.6.1) and 'the nominal APOGEE camera focal length of 356 mm' (W19 Sec. 13.6.2). The camera was built for a warmer design temperature than achieved (W19 Sec. 12.5).

Collimator focal length and collimated-beam diameter stated as such: f_col is DERIVED from the cold radius in Table 5 (R/2 = 1053.6 mm) and W from f_col/3.85 (273.7 mm), cross-checked by the VPH aperture (465 x cos 54 deg = 273.3 mm), the VPH mask (272.8 mm) and the camera pupil (356/1.3 = 273.8 mm).

The off-axis detector geometry in a form the explorer can use: Table 5 gives a 15 mm camera decentre, a -2.963 deg tilt and a 25.69 mm lateral offset of the green array, but not the wavelength at the mosaic centre. The lamC = 1.6158 um and camera angle 109.27 deg used here are DERIVED by fitting the published outer edges.
Chip-gap widths in wavelength: only the 2.9 mm physical gap and the chip edges rounded to 1 nm (gaps 40 and 30 A, DERIVED; the f tan theta model gives 50 and 42 A).
APOGEE-S per-chip wavelength coverage, dispersion and as-built VPH line density (W19 gives only the panel mismatch, 0.015-0.025 lines/mm, the 29.2" wedge and the resolution map, Table 13).
Fibre output focal ratio on the du Pont (f/7.5 input): only the expectation that FRD brings it close to APOGEE-N's (W19 Sec. 13.1).

Arns, J., et al. 2010, Proc. SPIE 7739, 773913 (the mosaic VPH paper, with the full grating requirements): no open copy found (SPIE Digital Library only; a search snippet of the PSU abstract page mentions a 290 mm x 475 mm elliptical grating -- not saved, not verified, not used).
Wilson, J. C., et al. 2010, Proc. SPIE 7735, 77351C and Wilson et al. 2012, Proc. SPIE 8446 (design-stage and early-performance papers): no open copies found.
Bowen & Vaughan 1973 (du Pont telescope): not retrieved; the du Pont aperture and f/7.5 come from W19 Sec. 13.1.
A published active-pixel format: 2040 x 2040 is DERIVED from N15's 4-px reference border; W19 quotes 2048 x 2048 and the 36.86 mm array size.
conflicts: VPH line density: 1008.6 /mm (design at 77 K; W19 Sec. 4.5) vs 1009.345 /mm (as recorded at room temperature; W19 Sec. 4.5 and Table 5 note k) vs 1009.524 /mm ('room - 200 K'; W19 Fig. 21 legend) vs 1009.3 grooves/mm (M17). The recommended preset uses 1009.345 with alpha = 54.061 deg (the as-built pairing in Table 5); the cold 1009.524 moves the Littrow wavelength by 2.8 A (1.6043 -> 1.6040 um) but, with lamC pinned at the mosaic centre, moves the modeled chip edges by < 0.1 nm (DERIVED).
Incidence angle: 54 deg (design; W19 Sec. 4.5, Fig. 24; M17) vs 54.061 deg (as built; W19 Table 5 note j, and Sec. 4.5 '+0.061 deg').
Littrow / centre wavelength: 1.6042 um (W19 Sec. 4.5, Littrow ghost) vs Littrow ghost at 1.6056-1.6067 um (M17 Table 2) vs '1.605 ± 10 microns' (DR16; the '10' cannot be microns).

Resolution per chip: W19 Table 1 medians 22,800 / 23,700 / 22,000 (blue / green / red) vs M17 Table 2 23,500 / 23,400 / 22,600 (at 1.54 / 1.61 / 1.66 um) vs nominal 22,500 (W19 abstract, N15 average, S3P). Within a chip R ranges from -6% to +12% about each fibre sample's median, and the medians differ by up to 15% between the top, middle and bottom fibres (green 22,200-25,500; W19 Table 11). APOGEE-S is lower, especially in the red (W19 Table 13).

Beam into the spectrograph: ~f/3.5 (95% EE; W19 Sec. 1, Sec. 3.3.2, Fig. 11, Table 9) vs f/3.0 Gaussian-apodised (Zemax model; W19 Sec. 4.7, Table 5 note d) vs clipped at ~f/3.7 (collimator mask) and ~f/3.85 (VPH mask) vs camera designed for f/4 (W19 Sec. 4.7).
Camera focal ratio: f/1.3 at f/3.85 illumination (W19 Sec. 4, Fig. 16) vs ~f/1.0 for the full clear aperture vs ~f/1.4 (W19 Sec. 4.6.1, depth-of-focus statement).
Collimator focal length (all DERIVED): 1053.6 mm (R/2) vs 1052.3 mm (slit-to-mirror path in Table 5) vs 1053.8 mm (2.96 x 356 mm).

Dispersion: 0.326 / 0.282 / 0.235 A/px (W19 Table 1, M17 Table 2) vs 'central dispersion' 0.326 / 0.283 / 0.236 A/pix (DR16). The f tan theta model matches at the chip centres (0.3257 / 0.2858 / 0.2354) but not at the literal 1.54 / 1.61 / 1.66 um (0.329 / 0.290 / 0.249), so the triplet is best read as chip-centre values.
Fibre pitch on the detector: 6.6 px (W19, M17) vs ~6.5 px between PSF peaks (DR16) vs 6-7 px (N15) vs ~7 px per spectrum in the design (M17 Sec. 2.7).

Spectral fibre-image width / LSF: ~1.7 px at 1.53 um to ~3.0 px at 1.68 um (W19 Sec. 4) vs LSF FWHM 2.01 / 2.44 / 3.14 px at 1.54 / 1.61 / 1.66 um (M17 Table 2) vs ~2.3 px nominal, < 2 px in the blue (S3P; W19 Sec. 13.6.2).
Dither step: commanded 0.5 px; measured mean 0.490 px (W19 Sec. 11.6); ~0.4 px in early survey data (N15; W19: 0.410 px for the first two months).
Fibre length: ~45-46 m (W19 Sec. 1, Fig. 1, Sec. 3.1) vs 40 m (N15 Sec. 1; S3P 'the single 40-m fiber run') -- irrelevant to the optics.
Predicted / measured throughput: 11 / 12 / 8% and 18% (W19 Table 1) vs 14 / 15 / 10% and 20 +/- 2% (M17 Table 2) -- not modeled by the explorer.
notes: Explorer mapping (DESI convention): D = 2.5 m with F = 3.85 makes f_col = W x F = 1053.6 mm; the entrance is the slit of equal line width, (sqrt3/2) x 120 um = 103.9 um, i.e. 2.227" at f/3.85. The true sky size is 2.0" (core at f/5); the arcsec number in the explorer is a collimator-side bookkeeping value. R, sampling and coverage do not depend on the F/W split as long as W x F = 1053.6 mm (F = 3.5, W = 301.0 mm gives the same results but a camera f/1.18 instead of the published f/1.3).

Detector: three 2048-px arrays along the dispersion with 2.9 mm (161 px) gaps. Entering Nx = 6466 (gaps as dead pixels) reproduces the outer edges 1.514-1.696 um; Nx = 6144 (gaps not modeled, as for the HIRES mosaic) gives 1.5194-1.6929 um, trimming 5.5 nm (blue) and 3.4 nm (red) from the ends (DERIVED). Wavelength decreases with pixel number on the real arrays (DR16: negative dispersion; chip a = red, chip c = blue).

Camera angle: the real camera points along the Littrow direction (deviation 108.122 deg as built) and the arrays sit off-axis (Table 5 notes m, q). The explorer centres the detector on the camera axis, so the preset aims the camera at the mosaic centre (lamC = 1.6158 um, beta = 55.21 deg, deviation 109.27 deg, DERIVED). With that choice the ideal f tan theta model reproduces all six published chip edges to within 1 nm and the published A/px at the chip centres to within 1.3%; the published 1.514-1.696 um span falls on 116.1 mm of the 116.4 mm mosaic, so the edges imply an effective f_cam within ~0.3% of 356 mm (DERIVED; edges rounded to 1 nm and varying by fibre), which supports using the warm-measured 356 mm.

Resolution: the slit-limited model R (~27,000-29,000 with the slit-equivalent width) exceeds the measured 22,000-23,700 because the delivered LSF (2.0-3.1 px FWHM, non-Gaussian; W19 Sec. 11.2-11.3, N15) includes pixelisation, residual astigmatism and focus errors. Using the full 120 um core gives 23,250-25,065.

Undersampling: the spectral fibre image is < 2 px in the blue; the survey takes exposure pairs dithered by 0.5 px and interleaves them (W19 Sec. 7.1, 11.6; N15 Sec. 6.5). The explorer's sampling numbers are the native (undithered) values.

Pseudo-slit: on a sphere of radius 1051.6 mm (half the collimator radius, the Schmidt condition) built as a polygon of 10 flat v-groove blocks, plus a 386 mm lateral curvature that straightens the monochromatic slit image (W19 Sec. 4.1); the slit is an obscuration in the collimated beam (M17). Fold 1 is used twice and bent into a weak cylinder to cancel astigmatism; Fold 2 carries a thermal-blocking dichroic (W19 Sec. 4.3-4.4).

APOGEE-S (du Pont, LCO): a near-copy with a two-panel VPH plus a 29.2" correction wedge, different cold-plate support and LN2 suspension, and somewhat lower resolution (W19 Sec. 13). On the du Pont the same 120 um core subtends 1.31" (f/7.5). Detector gains differ (1.9 vs 3.0 e-/DN, W19 Sec. 5.4.2).
Littrow ghost: falls at the Littrow wavelength (1.6042 um) because the fringes are untilted (W19 Sec. 4.5); the model's 1.6043 um checks G and alpha together.

Quotes: W19 and M17 render the double prime as '00' and the degree sign as U+25E6 in the text layer; these are written here as " and deg / ° and were matched after glyph normalisation. W19 table rows are quoted from the pdftotext -layout rows (superscript note letters such as 'Mirrorg' are part of the text layer).
